answer: A work-and-reputation gate resists fake identities: each new identity must first solve a unique compute puzzle and post a small refundable bond, so a Sybil farm pays per head, not once for many accounts. It then earns trust only by submitting original, graded work over many epochs, like tending an orchard rather than taking nectar in one visit. Its public graded history becomes a relic that follows its keypair, so clones with no history, identical timing, or copied text are flagged by juries and lose their bond. Attack cost grows with every identity, while honest reputation compounds.
